title: The Singhpuria misl

cards: The man with the fan. Earlier on this path you met him at Amritsar, fanning the sangat on a hot day, when the title of nawab found him. Nawab Kapur Singh went on to lead the Khalsa through the hard years.
But the title came to a man who already had home ground: his own village, his own riders, and they had a name. Today, not the title and not the fan. Today: the Singhpuria misl.

teach.b: Three pieces. A renamed village: tradition says Kapur Singh took a village called Faizullapur, near Amritsar, and renamed it Singhpura, the town of the Singhs.
His band took the new name, the Singhpurias, and some histories still call them by the old one, the Faizullapurias. The misl's name holds a small act of claiming.
The size of the band: in the way Sikh histories tell it, the Singhpurias were not among the great misls in riders or land. That's the surprise.

teach.h: A MODEST BAND FOR A NAWAB.
teach.b: The man who held the title of nawab, whom the chiefs followed through the hard century, led a modest band of his own. He could have used his place at the head of the Khalsa to make his own riders the strongest.
Tradition doesn't remember him doing that.
Who came after: when Kapur Singh grew old, tradition says, the leadership of the whole Khalsa did not pass to his own band. It went to Jassa Singh, of the Ahluwalias, the rider he had trained.

His misl carried on under its own chiefs, and the leadership of everyone went where he judged it should go. A nawab whose band stayed modest. A chief who handed the biggest job outside his own circle.
Sikh histories dwell on his humility: the fan, the stables, the robe touched to the feet of five Sikhs.
The Singhpuria misl is the same humility, written in the map.

how: Sikhs remember Nawab Kapur Singh in Sikh histories and gurdwara talks as a leader known for seva, and the Singhpuria misl as the band that came from his village.

games.q: you're Nawab Kapur Singh, growing old. your own riders would love to lead the whole Khalsa next. what do you do?
o: hand the leadership to your own band.
pass it to the rider you trained, from another band.
games.why: tradition says it went to Jassa Singh, from the Ahluwalias, while the Singhpurias carried on under their own chiefs.

practice: Think of a time you could have kept something and handed it on instead: a seat, a role, the last slice, a job a newer person got to try.
Or a time you held on; don't judge either, just let the moment come back, what it cost you and what it gave them. If you pray, breathe Waheguru as it settles.

wordCard.voice: Singhpura, the village Nawab Kapur Singh renamed, giving his own band the Singhpuria misl's name. This week: the Ramgarhias, the Kanhaiyas, the Sukerchakias, the Nakais, the Dallewalias, the Nishanwalias, and the Singhpurias. Today's word.
